**Research notes (today is Monday, Oct 12, 2026)**

- The TSX is closed today for Thanksgiving, so there is no trading and no live movement to report. Toronto trading resumes on October 13 at 9:30 a.m. ET after the Thanksgiving closure. A market-wrap article from today also says Toronto was closed for Thanksgiving, leaving the S&P/TSX Composite at Friday's 35,664.62.
- The most recent close was Friday, Oct 9, 2026. The S&P/TSX Composite Index closed at 35,664.62, up 519.24 points (1.477%). The TMX Money page shows that as the last trade, at 4:00 PM ET on Oct 9.
- Reasons given for Friday's rise:
  - Canada's September employment loss of 68,300 jobs, against a forecast gain of 9,200, reduced expectations for a Bank of Canada rate hike, Reuters reported.
  - Materials rose 2.81 percent, technology gained 2.88 percent and financials advanced 1.21 percent.
  - Aritzia was the strongest large mover, rising 20.5 percent after beating expectations for second-quarter revenue and profit.
- Weekly and longer-term context:
  - The index ended the week 0.46 percent higher after two weekly declines, The Globe and Mail reported.
  - Over the past month, the index has climbed 0.45% and is up 19.48% compared to the same time last year. That figure comes from Trading Economics. MSN Money instead shows a 1-month return of -0.09%, so the one-month figures differ by source.
  - The 52-week range is 29,530.92 to 37,069.11. CNBC dates the 52-week high to 08/26/26.
- Some results were stale or off-topic and were not used. These included a TradingView snippet citing about 24,050 and a Yahoo Finance page showing a different index.
